title: JSON Schema Generator and Validator Online | OpenAnyDoc
description: Generate a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) from your JSON, or validate JSON against a schema and jump to each error in the tree. Free, nothing uploaded.
heading: JSON Schema Generator and Validator
subtitle: Write a schema from your JSON, or check JSON against a schema; nothing is uploaded.
intro: A free JSON Schema tool: open a .json file, drop it or paste the text, and the page opens on the Schema tab. Generate a schema writes a JSON Schema in draft 2020-12 from your document, describing its keys and their types, ready to copy or download as a starting point. Or paste a schema you already have and validate the document against it: each error says what failed and links to the node in the tree. Everything runs in your browser and nothing is uploaded.

features.title: Errors you can find
features.text: Every validation error links to the node it is about, so you see the value in the tree at once.

features.title: Private and free
features.text: Your JSON and your schema are checked by your own browser and never sent to a server. No account, no watermark.

features.title: Works offline
features.text: Once this page has loaded, it keeps working without an internet connection.

stepsTitle: How it works: generate or validate a JSON Schema

steps.title: Open or paste your JSON
steps.text: Choose a .json file, drop it on the page, paste the text into the box, or try one of the two samples.

steps.title: Generate a schema
steps.text: On the Schema tab, press Generate a schema to get a draft 2020-12 schema of the document. Copy it or download it as a .json file.

steps.title: Or validate against your schema
steps.text: Paste a schema into the Schema tab instead. The document is checked against it, and each error links to its node in the tree.

handlesTitle: What the JSON Schema tool handles
handles: Schema generation in JSON Schema draft 2020-12, from the types and keys in your document.
Validation of the open document against a pasted schema, in your browser.
A list of errors, each linked to its node in the tree.
Copy or download the generated schema as a .json file.

limits: A generated schema describes the one document it was made from; review it and loosen or tighten rules before you rely on it.
A schema that refers to other schemas by web address cannot fetch them; paste a schema that holds everything it needs.
Files up to 10 MB, and both the document and the schema must be valid JSON.

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your JSON and your schema are read, generated and validated by your browser, on your device, and are never sent anywhere. Pasted text stays in this tab.

faq.question: What is a JSON Schema?
faq.answer: A JSON Schema is a JSON document that describes what another JSON document should look like: which keys it needs, the type of each value and which values are allowed. Programs use it to check data before they accept it.

faq.question: Which draft does the generated schema use?
faq.answer: Draft 2020-12, the current version of JSON Schema. The schema's $schema key says so, so tools that read it know which rules apply.

faq.question: Is the generated schema ready to use as it is?
faq.answer: It is a starting point. It is written from one example, so it cannot know which keys are optional elsewhere or which values are allowed; read it and adjust it to your rules.

faq.question: Can my schema use $ref to another file?
faq.answer: Only references inside the pasted schema itself. Nothing is fetched from the internet, so a $ref to a web address cannot be followed; put the referenced definitions into the schema you paste.

faq.question: How do I find the part of my JSON that failed?
faq.answer: Every error is listed on the Schema tab, and each one links to its node in the tree, so you can jump straight to the value that broke the rule.

faq.question: How do I generate a JSON Schema from a JSON sample?
faq.answer: Open or paste a sample in OpenAnyDoc's JSON Schema tool and press Generate a schema on the Schema tab to get a draft 2020-12 schema you can copy or download. Treat it as a starting point, since it is written from one example; it is made in your browser without uploading.
